note: Public pieces require a named creator, a resolvable HTTPS work source, and production evidence. Empty prompt arrays mean the creator did not publish exact prompts; they are not reconstructed.

pieces.title: Air Head
pieces.synopsis: A man with a yellow balloon for a head reflects on the strange practicalities and possibilities of his life.

workflow_steps: Write a short script and define the story beats before generating.
Generate a large pool of Sora clips from many goal-specific prompts.
Edit the material like documentary footage, selecting moments that serve the scripted beats.
Use conventional VFX, rotoscoping, sound design, colour correction, and editorial timing to finish the film.

prompts.text: Man with a yellow balloon for a head. 35mm film.

pieces.historic_tool_note: Made with a tool that is no longer available.

pieces.title: The Hardest Part
pieces.synopsis: An unbroken dreamlike journey moves through a couple’s imagined life, memory, loss, and the impossibility of going back.

workflow_steps: Return to a decade-old concept built around an impossible continuous zoom through a couple’s life.
Write detailed Sora prompts that specify imagery, shot angle, movement, and spatial transitions.
Generate short scenes and select transitions that can carry the forward zoom.
Direct and edit the generated scenes into one continuous memory journey set to the finished Washed Out track.

prompts.text: We zoom through the bubble it pops and we zoom through the bubblegum and enter an open football field.

pieces.historic_tool_note: Made with a tool that is no longer available.

pieces.title: The Frost
pieces.synopsis: A remote expedition encounters an uncanny frozen world assembled from AI-generated still imagery.

workflow_steps: Start from Josh Rubin’s written screenplay.
Prompt and curate DALL·E 2 stills, using inpainting and outpainting to build each shot.
Cut images into layers and animate them with puppetry, After Effects-style compositing, and D-ID facial motion.
Assemble the quasi-video shots into the finished science-fiction sequence.
problems_and_solutions: DALL·E 2 struggled with precise emotional facial responses; the filmmakers stopped fighting for photographic precision and built the film around the model’s uncanny aesthetic.

pieces.historic_tool_note: Made with DALL·E 2, which is no longer available.

pieces.title: Thank You For Not Answering
pieces.synopsis: A voicemail opens into fragments of memory and an imagined life that never happened.

workflow_steps: Write the voicemail-led script.
Generate short image- and text-prompted clips in Runway Gen-2.
Curate the model’s aberrations and unexpected images instead of forcing realism.
Edit the fragments into a subjective memory flow around the spoken message.
problems_and_solutions: The generated footage produced surreal side effects and aberrations; Trillo treated those accidents as the film’s visual language rather than defects to erase.

pieces.historic_tool_note: Made with Runway Gen-2, which is no longer available.

pieces.title: PLSTC
pieces.synopsis: An underwater dystopia confronts the damage plastic pollution causes to marine life.

workflow_steps: Build a sequence around the environmental premise.
Generate ocean-creature imagery with Midjourney.
Hand-composite and animate the selected images with conventional digital tools.
Finish with dedicated music, sound design, and mix.

pieces.title: Hairy Pouter
pieces.synopsis: A grandmother’s idiosyncratic book review is interpreted through an early AI image generator.

workflow_steps: Select recorded review excerpts from the director’s grandmother.
Enter her words into early Midjourney without adding franchise context.
Identify a compelling generated art direction and guide later images toward that thread.
Edit the still-image progression to the original narration with human sound and music.
problems_and_solutions: The first generations varied wildly; the team wrote down the visual hallmarks of a successful image and reused that direction to keep the sequence readable and consistent.

pieces.title: Sunspring
pieces.synopsis: Three performers enact a surreal science-fiction screenplay written by a recurrent neural network.

workflow_steps: Train an LSTM recurrent neural network on science-fiction screenplays.
Supply the 48-hour challenge requirements and generate the screenplay.
Interpret the generated stage directions with actors and a conventional film crew.
Shoot and finish the short within the festival deadline.

pieces.historic_tool_note: Written with a custom historic LSTM model that is not a public service.

pieces.title: The Script

creator.name: Aturi, Lucía Clavijo, and Victor Martinez

pieces.synopsis: A compact short created under a 48-hour generative-film constraint.

workflow_steps: Write and plan the short within the Gen:48 deadline.
Generate the images in Midjourney.
Animate the selected images with Runway Gen-3 Alpha.
Edit and finish the film before the 48-hour cutoff.

pieces.historic_tool_note: Made with Runway Gen-3 Alpha, which has been superseded.

pieces.title: Grow
pieces.synopsis: A short about learning to cope with life and letting go, made during a 48-hour challenge.

workflow_steps: Develop the story and prompts inside the 48-hour limit.
Generate still images with Leonardo.Ai.
Turn those images into video with Runway Gen-3.
Assemble the complete short before the challenge deadline.

pieces.historic_tool_note: Made with Runway Gen-3, which has been superseded.

pieces.title: Instant
pieces.synopsis: An anachronistic dialogue considers time and the ways people perceive it.

workflow_steps: Shape the dialogue-driven idea for the Gen:48 constraint.
Generate occasional supporting images with Stable Diffusion.
Create the scenes end to end with Runway Gen-1 and Gen-2.
Build sound effects and score, then finish the edit.

pieces.historic_tool_note: Made primarily with Runway Gen-1/Gen-2, which are no longer available.

pieces.title: Caspah
pieces.synopsis: A grandmother’s remembered horror films become a playful, personal ghost-story collage.

workflow_steps: Return to recorded conversations about the creator’s grandmother’s favorite scary films.
Use Google Flow within the Flow Sessions program to interpret those memories as scenes.
Direct for character, cinematography, and story while staying open to unexpected generations.
Edit the generated material around the original personal recordings.

pieces.title: Last Stand
pieces.synopsis: Humanity responds to apparent extraterrestrial contact in an AI-assisted science-fiction scenario.

workflow_steps: Use Brightpen to assist with the screenplay.
Generate concept art and synthetic voices through the same credited service.
Make human editorial and creative decisions around the generated material.
Assemble the science-fiction short with an original score.

pieces.historic_tool_note: Made with Brightpen, a service that is no longer reliably available.
